analysis: Reviewed the only change in provider-swift/Sources/ProviderCore/ProviderLoop+ModelLoading.swift: unloadModel (head ~1133-1137 and ~1200-1203). After a successful Nemotron Super slot retirement, and after a normal unload completes, it now calls selectedModelRecovery.makeAllDue(now: .now). This marks waiting selected-model recovery entries as due so they are rechecked at the next capacity tick. The change adds no new network input, no new key/plaintext handling, and no new persistence. It touches no attestation, authorization (TB-011/T-053), coordinator-wire (TB-002) or prefix-cache storage (T-041) code paths. Impact is limited to scheduling: after an unload, selected-model load retries run sooner. Any DoS or thrash risk would depend on the unseen selectedModelRecovery implementation, which was not supplied. The retry attempts still pass through the existing ensureModelLoaded gates (retirement, autopilot ownership, memory admission, runtime eligibility), so I found no bypass. The unload paths that return false (autopilot pins, retained MTP, GLM retirement fault) never reach makeAllDue. The early return for native MiMo retirement is unchanged, so it doesn't trigger recovery. Open question for integration: whether makeAllDue is bounded/rate-limited, and whether eviction-driven unloads could cause repeated load/evict cycles between selected models. This is an availability/performance concern, not a demonstrated vulnerability. Source of SelectedModelRecovery and its caller was not supplied.
